key_insight: SARLO-80 introduces a large-scale, very-high-resolution SAR–optical dataset built to better support multimodal foundation models. Unlike many prior resources, it preserves native SAR measurements and acquisition geometry, enabling more physically grounded learning.
problem_solved: Current SAR–optical datasets are often low-resolution, intensity-only, and based on GRD products, which lose important SAR information such as complex-valued signals and imaging geometry. This limits the development of robust multimodal AI models for SAR analysis.
method: Assemble a worldwide dataset pairing slant-range SAR data with optical imagery at 80 cm resolution.
Preserve complex-valued SAR measurements and native acquisition geometry instead of reducing SAR to intensity-only GRD representations.
Provide a large-scale benchmark designed for physically consistent multimodal learning across SAR and optical modalities.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this dataset offers a stronger foundation for training and evaluating models that fuse SAR and optical data. It can improve downstream tasks where resolution, sensor geometry, and physical fidelity matter, such as remote sensing, Earth observation, and robust multimodal perception.
